texts.preamble: Mahavir S/O. Mulchand Darda vs The State Of Maharashtra on 13 February, 2020 Author: Mangesh S. Patil Bench: Mangesh S. Patil 910 aba 1501 19.odt In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay Bench At Aurangabad Anticipatory Bail Application No. 1501 Of 2019 Mahavir s/o Mulchand Darda, Age 58 years, Occ. Business, R/o. Nanded. ... Applicant. Versus State of Maharashtra, Through Vajirabad Police Station, Nanded. ... Respondent. ... Advocate for the Applicant : Mr. D.S. Bharuka. App for the Respondent/State : Mr. V.S. Badakh. Coram : Mangesh S. Patil, J. Date : 13/02/2020 Per Court : The applicant is seeking bail in anticipation of his arrest in connection with Crime No. 17/2019, registered with Vazirabad Police Station, Nanded, for the offences punishable under Section 188, 272, 273, 328 of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 59 of the Food, Safety and Standards Act, 2006. 2. The applicant is stated to have been found in possession of scented tobacco, Ghutka, Panmasala etc. which was seized.
texts.facts: The applicant is seeking bail in anticipation of his arrest in connection with Crime No. 17/2019, registered with Vazirabad Police Station, Nanded, for the offences punishable under Section 188, 272, 273, 328 of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 59 of the Food, Safety and Standards Act, 2006. 2. The applicant is stated to have been found in possession of scented tobacco, Ghutka, Panmasala etc. which was seized. Samples were drawn. F.I.R. was lodged by an officer under the Food and Safety Act. The crime was registered for the aforementioned sections.
texts.arguments: 3. The learned advocate for the applicant submits that since there are no allegations about the substance having been administered 910 aba 1501 19.odt to anybody, the Provisions of Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code would not be attracted. The rest of the offences being bailable, the muddemal having been already seized, custodial interrogation of the applicant is not necessary. He is ready to abide by all the terms and conditions and may be granted bail. The learned A.P.P. opposes the application. He submits that there is a genuine dispute as to the applicability of Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 3. The learned advocate for the applicant submits that since there are no allegations about the substance having been administered 910 aba 1501 19.odt to anybody, the Provisions of Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code would not be attracted. He is ready to abide by all the terms and conditions and may be granted bail. The learned A.P.P. opposes the application. He submits that there is a genuine dispute as to the applicability of Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code.
